subject: Observability ingest auth patterns, buffer sizing and trace-sampling plan for private deploy
messages:
From: infra@acmecorp.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability on-prem integration for Redwood private deploy

Hi Connor,

We're standing up the Redwood Private deployment in our us-west-2 VPC next week. Security asked us to confirm the recommended pattern for shipping logs/metrics/traces from the private cluster to our SIEM (Splunk) and for how Redwood expects customers to wire tracing hooks so we can correlate user-facing requests with model traces. A few constraints:

- Egress is tightly restricted (only outbound to approved FQDNs/IP ranges over TCP 443 and TCP 8088 allowed).
- We prefer mutual TLS for long-lived connections but can accept short-lived bearer tokens if mTLS is too heavy operationally.
- We need a defensible chain-of-custody: signed receipts or attestations for evidence bundles we hand to security during audits.
- Disk-spool allowed up to 10GB for forwarder buffering.

Specific asks:
1) Auth pattern recommendation (mTLS vs short-lived HEC tokens + rotation).
2) Suggested buffer sizing & retry/backoff policy for the forwarder under 100MB/s burst.
3) Trace sampling guidance (target RPS ~ 350 requests/s at peak).
4) Example log JSON for request/response events and how to surface Redwood trace IDs for correlation.

Thanks — can you sketch a recommended plan we can use in the runbook?

Regards,
Alice Chen
Senior Cloud Infra Engineer
AcmeCorp

From: connor_obrien@redwood.example.com
To: infra@acmecorp.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability on-prem integration for Redwood private deploy

Alice — thanks for the detail, this is a great framing. High-level recommendation up front: opt for mTLS for persistent SIEM ingestion where you control both ends; fall back to short-lived HEC tokens (rotated via a secure STS flow) when mTLS can't be provisioned. Below is an operational plan and concrete defaults you can paste into the runbook.

1) Auth patterns (recommended order):
- mTLS (preferred): use a client cert issued by AcmeCorp PKI. We support standard TLS mutual authentication to Splunk HEC or a customer-owned forwarder. mTLS provides the cleanest chain-of-custody (cert identity + mutual verification).
- Short-lived HEC tokens: if mTLS impossible, use HEC tokens that are rotated every 1 hour via an automated STS/OIDC flow. Tokens should be minted by a short-lived credentials service; rotate on failure/restart.
- Signed receipts: regardless of auth, enable HMAC-signed delivery receipts from your on-prem forwarder. We recommend signing each evidence packet with an HSM-backed key and storing the signature in an audit log.

2) Forwarder topology and buffer sizing:
- Deploy the OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) as a dedicated, highly-available pair (2 replicas) in each AZ. Forwarder will accept local syslog and file-based exports from Redwood components and export to Splunk HEC or syslog-ng endpoint.
- Buffering: allow 10GB filesystem spool (you stated this is OK). With 100MB/s burst capacity target, use a disk spool with a 5x safety multiplier and a 300s max retry window. Config suggestion: write-ahead queue with 1GB memory buffer and filesystem spool rollover at 2GB chunks to avoid large file locks.
- Retry/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter; initial retry 1s, max backoff 120s. Circuit-breaker: if persistent 5xxs for >10 minutes, mark the endpoint degraded and switch to a secondary egress endpoint (see firewall rules below).

3) Trace sampling and correlation:
- Default: 0.5% probabilistic sampling at ingress to protect backend storage.
- Adaptive tail sampling: enable tail-based sampling in the OTel collector using a 5-minute evaluation window for high-value requests (errors, latency outliers, high-cost token usage). For your 350 RPS peak we recommend a baseline of 1% with a 25% adaptive boost for error traces.
- Trace IDs: Redwood injects a span attribute redwood.request_id and populates W3C traceparent. Make sure your SIEM mapping flattens traceparent into a tracing_id field to allow joins between logs and spans. Example: redwood.request_id=rw-3f9a2b.

4) Example log schema (JSON) for request/response event (single line JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-08-12T09:12:34.123Z",
  "service": "redwood-inference",
  "env": "prod-us-west-2",
  "redwood_request_id": "rw-3f9a2b",
  "traceparent": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01",
  "request_path": "/v1/generate",
  "duration_ms": 312,
  "tokens_in": 54,
  "tokens_out": 312,
  "model": "openlm-gpt-13b",
  "level": "info"
}

(We recommend single-line JSON objects to simplify indexing in Splunk; include traceparent and redwood_request_id for joins.)

5) Firewall / egress rules:
- Allow outbound to the following endpoints from forwarder IPs only:
  * splunk-hec.acmecorp.internal:443 (mTLS)
  * splunk-hec-failover.acmecorp.internal:443
  * redwood-obsv-auth.us-west-2.redwood.example.com:443 (token minting/STS)
- If you run a proxy/egress gateway, configure health checks (TCP 443) and permit sustained connections.

6) Acceptance criteria & evidence for audits:
- Demonstrate TLS mutual-auth handshake logs for a 24h window.
- Show signed receipts for a set of 10 sampled evidence packets; signatures must validate against a known HSM public key.
- Trace correlation test: generate synthetic requests with known traceparents and show they join with logs in Splunk within 2 minutes.

I'll attach a sample OTel config and an evidence-checklist for your audit team. If you want, we can run a 2-hour validation call to step through the proof-of-concept.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in compliance — thanks Connor. Quick operational notes and attachments below.

- I've attached an evidence-checklist.pdf with the exact artifacts we recommend collecting for SOC-type assessments (TLS cert chains, forwarder config, HSM key thumbprints, signed receipts).
- Attached obsv-config-sample.yaml is a minimalist OTel collector config tuned for your 350 RPS baseline (includes tail-sampler rules and disk_spool settings).
- Retention: confirm whether Acme wants 90/365/730-day hot/warm policies. Our default guidance for regulated customers is 365 days hot, 2 years cold.

Please confirm the retention window and whether you have an internal cert authority we should trust for mTLS. If you prefer, we can pre-generate a CSR template for your PKI team.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF, 240KB); obsv-config-sample.yaml (YAML, 4KB)]
